title: Thruster CAD and Stress Analyst
description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building innovative aerospace technologies that advance the future of space transportation.

The heart of a spacecraft lies in its propulsion system, and that's why we, at The Exploration Company, are dedicated to developing our own cutting-edge Propulsion Systems ensuring the highest level of efficiency and reliability in our space endeavours.

We want you as a talented CAD & Stress Analyst to help us in our mission by designing and structurally justifying the hardware that makes up our propulsion systems, with a particular focus on the Thrust Chamber Assembly(TCA). You will own parts from initial CAD layout through to final stress justification, working hand in hand with the manufacturing and test teams to bring flight hardware from concept to qualified design.

Key responsibilities

In your capacity as a CAD & Stress Analyst, you will be responsible for the on-time and on-cost design and structural justification of propulsion hardware, with the TCA as your primary scope.

Your role will be continuously evolving, but day-to-day responsibilities will include:

During the Design Phase:

  • Design the thrust chamber & injector propulsion hardware in CAD, from concept layout through to detailed design.

  • Perform stress analysis (hand calculations and FEA) on designed parts to substantiate margins of safety under mechanical, thermal and pressure loads.

  • Select materials and define manufacturing processes in coordination with manufacturing engineering, accounting for structural, thermal and producibility constraints.

  • Work closely with propulsion, thermal and fluidic system engineers to translate functional requirements into part-level design and load cases.

  • Establish and maintain interface definitions, drawings and part datasets, ensuring configuration control and traceability.

  • Conduct trade studies on design options (geometry, material, manufacturing route) and justify design decisions with analysis.

  • Elaborate and maintain structural analysis reports supporting design reviews and qualification.

  • Support the definition of test requirements needed to validate analytical models and structural assumptions.

  • Produce and maintain technical documentation of design choices and trade-offs, to a high standard, capturing analysis methods and results as to serve as reference justification for the design.

During Manufacturing, Assembly and Test Phase:

  • Support manufacturing and inspection of parts, resolving design or tolerance issues as they arise.

  • Support root-cause investigations of any structural anomaly or test finding, correlating analysis with hardware behaviour.

  • Update and correlate stress models and analyses based on test and inspection results.

  • Support design iterations and upgrades based on test campaign outcomes.

About the role:

We're hiring for Self-Managed Experience (SMX) — the team responsible for making Camunda 8 deployable in a self-service way for customers who run their own infrastructure. SMX covers two areas of work: installation artifacts (Helm chart, Docker Compose, C8Run) and reference architectures & cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, Azure).

This role sits primarily on the installation artifacts side — building, maintaining, and releasing the artifacts that ship Camunda 8 to every self-managed customer. You'll be fully embedded in that area day-to-day, but you'll work alongside the reference-architecture side of the team regularly, and SMX is actively working toward enabling every engineer to review and contribute across both stacks over time.

SMX is also shifting from a purely artifact- and ops-focused team toward one in which engineers bring customer judgment and product sense alongside technical depth. That means engaging directly with the teams closest to customers — Support, Consulting, Presales — and using that signal to help shape what we prioritize, not just executing a fully-specced ticket.

You'll find plenty of room to leave your own footprint: deployment automation, software and infrastructure testing, multi-region setups, and developer experience are all live areas of investment as the team matures from "basic install" toward full-lifecycle ownership (upgrades, backup/restore, disaster recovery).

Curious about the kind of challenges you'll work on at Camunda? Watch this quick 30-minute talk from our engineers to learn more about the new Camunda Exporter and how we’re solving complex problems at scale

What You’ll Be Doing:

  •  Build, maintain, and release C8 distribution artifacts for self-managed customers — Helm Charts (Kubernetes), C8Run, and Docker Compose — along with their documentation.

  • Improve the reliability and usability of deployment artifacts across the full customer lifecycle: installation, upgrades, and day-2 operations, not just initial deployment.

  • Engage directly with internal customer-facing teams (Support, Consulting, Presales) to understand real deployment problems, and use that signal to help shape what gets prioritized — not just how it gets built. Collaborate with Development Teams, Product Management, QA, and Documentation to ship integrated, tested, and documented releases.

  • Take part in the team's shared medic rotation and resolve engineering-level support cases, feeding learnings back into development.

  • Contribute to the shared tooling (review, deployment, and test tooling) that SMX is building so other Camunda teams can adopt it — this is one of the team's current investment areas.

What success looks like (first ~3 months):

  • Taken on your first medic rotation slot and support tickets to understand the stack, customer challenges, and deployment environments.

  • Improved onboarding or documentation, turning your own ramp-up experience into concrete improvements.

  • Contributed to artifact fixes, CI/CD enhancements, or test automation that strengthens release quality.

  • Deliver structural improvement initiatives — a feature request, or a test/release improvement.

  • Built working relationships with engineering, QA, and product peers, and started building context on the reference-architecture side of the team.

  • Started forming your own view of a customer pain point from firsthand signal (support tickets, consulting feedback), not just from a ticket description.

What You Bring:

  • Ability and/or willingness to use our product, with genuine curiosity about the customer problem behind a ticket — comfortable asking "should we build this" as well as "how do we build this."

  • Ability to create clear technical documentation and communicate effectively across teams.

  • A pragmatic and autonomous approach to programming and problem-solving.

  • You thrive as a manager of one — you build it, you own it — and take pride in delivering maintainable, operable software.

  • Familiarity with Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, or similar observability tools.

  • Working knowledge of the Go programming language.

  • Exposure to cloud infrastructure/IaC (Terraform, Crossplane) — useful as SMX moves toward shared review capability across installation artifacts and reference architectures.

title: Ingénieur·e en médiation scientifique et valorisation de la recherche
description:
1-     ENVIRONNEMENT DU POSTE

Grande école d’ingénieur généraliste de l’IMT-Institut Mines-Télécom, premier groupe d’écoles d’ingénieurs de France, IMT Atlantique a pour ambition d’accompagner les transitions, de former des ingénieurs responsables et mettre l'excellence scientifique et technique au service de l'enseignement, de la recherche et de l'innovation.

Le poste est rattaché au Département interdisciplinaire en sciences sociales (DI2S) rassemblant des enseignants chercheurs et enseignantes chercheuses en sciences de gestion, sociologie, économie et droit. Sur le campus de Nantes, les recherches sont focalisées sur l’analyse des transformations des organisations et des métiers dans des systèmes sociotechniques. Trois domaines d’investigation sont privilégiés : l’industrie, la santé et l’environnement. Le ou la candidate sera affilé·e au LEMNA (Laboratoire Économie et Management Nantes Atlantique).

Plus précisément, le poste sera rattaché à la chaire RESOH [Recherche en Sécurité Organisations Hommes]. Les travaux de recherche, à l’interface de la sociologie et de la gestion, portent sur le fonctionnement des organisations à hauts risques. Partant de l’analyse du travail et des organisations de travail, il s’agit d’éclairer les dimensions socio-organisationnelles, managériales et institutionnelles contribuant à (ou empêchant) le maintien d’un niveau de fiabilité compatible avec les exigences de sécurité et de production. Les recherches de la chaire sont conduites en étroite collaboration avec des partenaires industriels et institutionnels. Elles visent à produire des connaissances scientifiques fondées sur des enquêtes de terrain, mais également à favoriser leur mise en discussion, leur appropriation et leur mobilisation par les acteurs concernés. Dans ce contexte, la chaire souhaite renforcer ses capacités de valorisation, de diffusion et d’appropriation de ses travaux, auprès de ses partenaires actuels comme, plus largement, du monde socio-économique.

 

2-     MISSIONS

En collaboration avec l’ensemble des enseignants-chercheurs de l’équipe (permanents et associés), les missions sont :

1-     Participer à la dynamique collective de recherche au sein de la chaire

2-     Structurer et valoriser les résultats des recherches de la chaire

3-     En favoriser l’appropriation par les partenaires industriels et institutionnels de la chaire (volet interne)

4-     Contribuer au rayonnement de la chaire auprès du monde socio-économique (volet externe)

 

 

3-     ACTIVITÉS : Activité par mission

 

  1.     Participer à la dynamique collective de recherche au sein de la chaire

·     contribue activement aux réunions de coordination, espaces de discussion et séminaires de recherche (au sein de l’équipe de recherche RESOH et avec les partenaires)

 

2.     Valoriser et diffuser les résultats des recherches de la chaire

·     cartographie les principaux travaux, résultats et productions de la chaire ;

·     identifie les publics susceptibles d’être intéressés par ces résultats ;

·     analyse leurs besoins et leurs attentes ;

·     contribue à définir des stratégies de valorisation et de communication adaptées aux différents projets ;

·     contribue à l’organisation des événements scientifiques (journée d’étude, colloque, etc.) ;

·     transforme les résultats scientifiques en ressources accessibles à des publics non spécialistes, sans en perdre la rigueur, la nuance ni la portée scientifique (synthèses, notes de recherche, fiches thématiques, supports de présentation, contenus numériques ou autres formats adaptés aux publics visés).

 

3.     Favoriser l’appropriation des travaux de recherche par les partenaires industriels et institutionnels de la chaire (volet interne)

·     prépare et organise des restitutions de travaux ;

·     conçoit et anime des ateliers ou temps d’échange ;

·     prépare des supports adaptés aux préoccupations des partenaires ;

·     recueille leurs réactions, questions et besoins ;

·     fait remonter vers les chercheurs les questions et attentes exprimées par les partenaires ;

·     contribue à identifier les conditions favorisant l’appropriation des résultats.

 

4.     Contribuer au rayonnement de la chaire auprès du monde socio-économique (volet externe)

·     identifie des organisations, réseaux et acteurs susceptibles d’être intéressés par les travaux de la chaire ;

·     développe et entretient des relations avec des acteurs industriels, institutionnels et professionnels ;

·     identifie des événements pertinents ;

·     prépare la participation de la chaire à des événements professionnels et scientifiques ;

·     participe à l’organisation d’événements scientifiques de la chaire (colloque, conférence, journée d’étude)

·     contribue à développer de nouveaux formats de rencontre entre chercheurs et praticiens ;

·     participe à la constitution de communautés d’intérêt autour de certaines thématiques de recherche.


Niveau de formation et/ou expérience minimums souhaité :

description:
Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable. Une école d’excellence où chacun a l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain.

Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif.

L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.

Transitions numériques, écologiques, industrielles : les grands défis de notre époque sont aussi ceux de l’Institut Henri Fayol.

Ici se mêlent Informatique, Sciences des données, Management, Sciences humaines et sociales, Génie environnemental pour penser les systèmes complexes de demain : territoires, entreprises, filières industrielles. 

📊 Résilience, performance, durabilité… Nous développons et expérimentons en lien étroit avec les acteurs socio-économique pour répondre aux exigences des transitions actuelles.

✨ Une recherche interdisciplinaire à fort impact, où l’humain est toujours au centre. 

Cette thèse de doctorat sera rattachée au département Génie de l'Environnement pour les Organisations (GEO), membre du Laboratoire CNRS UMR 5600 Environnement Ville et Société (EVS). Pour répondre aux enjeux des transitions écologique, énergétique et industrielle, le département GEO accompagne les acteurs des territoires (acteurs publics et privés) vers une meilleure prise en compte des enjeux environnementaux et de résilience territoriale. Il s'attache ainsi à apporter des solutions nouvelles en matière d'analyse, de modélisation et d'évaluation environnementale des systèmes industriels et territoriaux dans un double contexte d'industrie des futurs et de villes et territoires soutenables.

🏠 Contexte

Présentation du sujet

Le changement climatique met en lumière, comme l'a fait auparavant la crise COVID, les vulnérabilités et liens de dépendance généralisée de nos modes de vie envers les infrastructures, les chaînes de valeur, et modes d'organisation économique et technique, éléments souvent déconnectés de l'usager final, de ses besoins et des conditions d'occupation. Pour le secteur du bâtiment, Cimerman (2023) évoque une tendance depuis plusieurs décennies de « simplification cartésienne » de la conception et de l'opération du bâti. Celle-ci se traduit notamment par le développement d'un imaginaire de « bâtiment-machine », se traduisant par une superposition d'éléments techniques complexes (chauffage, ventilation, climatisation), susceptibles d'être pilotés au travers d'outils informatiques et d'une gestion centralisée optimisée (Cimerman, 2023).

Face aux enjeux posés par le changement climatique, deux voies opposées d'adaptation du bâti se dessinent. La première, actuellement dominante, consiste à prolonger cet imaginaire de « bâtiment-machine », rationalisable, mesurable et optimisable, et ce notamment au travers du développement du « smart-building ». Cette approche technosolutionniste apporte des réponses clés-en-main (capteurs, outils de pilotage centralisés, etc.) aux gestionnaires et usagers de bâtiments. Néanmoins, elle présente certains défis pour leur maintenance et leur entretien. Nous pouvons citer le recours massif aux nouvelles technologies, coûteuses, complexes, rapidement obsolètes et dont la fabrication repose en grande partie sur des ressources finies. Cela pose de plus les questions centrales des compétences, de la délégation du savoir et des outils associés à des opérateurs experts externes.

En contrepoint à la première voie, une seconde approche, encore marginale, émerge : celle d'un « bâtiment low-tech ». Popularisée ces dernières années en France par Philippe Bihouix (Bihouix, 2014), la low-tech questionne le rapport à la technologie et aux différentes formes de dépendances qu'elle génère (Tanguy et al., 2023). Dans le secteur du bâtiment, l'application de cette démarche renvoie souvent à la dépendance à la ressource (énergie et matière) : repenser les usages, l'origine des matériaux (réemployés, biosourcés) ou encore la simplicité de l'équipement utilisé. Bien que nécessaires, ces travaux s'intéressent pourtant peu à d'autres formes de dépendances associées à la technique, au titre desquelles nous pouvons citer la dépendance aux savoirs et aux formes d'organisation sociale et économique qui conditionnent l'adéquation, la pérennité et l'efficacité des solutions proposées.

Cette thèse offre ainsi une immersion concrète dans les questions d'adaptation du parc bâti au changement climatique par la « lowtech » à l'interface entre sciences de l'ingénieur et sciences humaines et sociales. Les compétences et l'expérience acquises trouveront une résonance particulière dans un secteur en pleine mutation, où la maîtrise des dépendances techniques, économiques et organisationnelles devient un enjeu central pour la soutenabilité des bâtiments et de leur exploitation.

Contexte scientifique

La littérature consacrée à la low-tech s'est structurée ces dernières années autour d'une critique de la fuite en avant technologique et des dépendances qu'elle engendre (Bihouix, 2014 ; Tanguy et al., 2023). Appliquée au bâtiment, cette littérature reste toutefois majoritairement centrée sur la phase de conception et sur la dépendance à la ressource : sobriété énergétique, choix de matériaux biosourcés ou réemployés, réduction du niveau d'équipement technique.

Deux angles morts en découlent. Le premier concerne la phase d'exploitation : la maintenance et l'entretien, qui représentent pourtant l'essentiel de la durée de vie d'un bâtiment et conditionnent la performance réelle des solutions installées, sont peu traités comme objet de recherche à part entière. Le second concerne la nature même des dépendances étudiées. Au-delà de la ressource, la conduite d'une opération de maintenance mobilise des savoirs et savoir-faire, des outils de diagnostic, des pièces détachées, des prestataires et des chaînes d'approvisionnement, ainsi que des cadres contractuels et réglementaires. Ces dépendances d’ordres cognitives, organisationnelles, économiques restent largement implicites et sous développées dans les travaux existants.

La caractérisation de ces dépendances soulève par ailleurs une question d'échelle. Analysée au seul niveau du bâtiment, la maintenance apparaît comme une somme d'opérations techniques ; replacée à l'échelle urbaine, elle révèle des réseaux d'acteurs, des filières, des compétences localement disponibles ou absentes, et des effets de dépendance mutualisés.

Contexte opérationnel

Du côté des acteurs institutionnels et économiques, de nombreux outils accompagnent aujourd'hui la gestion technique du patrimoine bâti. Nous pouvons citer :

  • les outils de gestion de maintenance assistée par ordinateur (GMAO) et les plateformes de gestion technique du bâtiment (GTB) ;

  • les démarches de modélisation des données du bâtiment (BIM d'exploitation, jumeaux numériques) et les labels associés à la connectivité des bâtiments ;

  • les contrats d'exploitation et de maintenance externalisés, et les dispositifs de garantie de performance énergétique ;

  • les démarches et retours d'expérience issus de la mouvance low-tech (chantiers démonstrateurs, guides praticiens, réseaux associatifs).

Ces dispositifs partagent une orientation commune : ils visent à optimiser la conduite de la maintenance, rarement à interroger les dépendances qu'elle installe. Les démarches low-tech, à l'inverse, portent cette interrogation mais restent au stade de l'expérimentation ponctuelle, sans cadre d'évaluation partagé ni capacité de généralisation à l'échelle d'un parc ou d'un territoire.

Il en résulte, en l'état des connaissances aussi bien scientifiques qu'opérationnelles, qu'il n'existe pas de méthode permettant de rendre visibles et de qualifier les dépendances associées à la maintenance et à l'entretien des bâtiments, ni d'évaluer dans quelle mesure une approche low-tech permettrait de les réduire.


🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous

Démarche de la thèse

L'objectif principal de cette thèse est de caractériser les apports d'une approche low-tech pour cartographier et maîtriser, sinon réduire, les différentes formes de dépendances associées à la maintenance et à l'entretien des bâtiments.

Les dépendances analysées s'appuieront sur les techniques, pratiques, outils et réseaux en lien avec la maintenance qui seront mis en évidence dans les deux autres thèses du projet PERENNIS. Cette thèse s'inscrit donc en complète continuité de ces deux travaux.

Dans un premier temps, il s'agira de construire un cadre d'analyse des dépendances liées à la maintenance du bâtiment, articulant quatre registres : les ressources (énergie, matière, pièces détachées), les savoirs et savoir-faire, les acteurs et leurs relations contractuelles, et les réseaux techniques et logistiques. Cette phase s'appuiera sur une revue de la littérature scientifique et « grise », sur un benchmark des pratiques et outils de maintenance existants, et sur des entretiens avec les acteurs du secteur (gestionnaires de patrimoine, bailleurs, mainteneurs, bureaux d'études, collectivités).

Dans un deuxième temps, ce cadre sera mobilisé pour caractériser et rendre visibles les schémas de dépendance à l'échelle urbaine, sur un ou plusieurs territoires d'étude. Il s'agira notamment d'identifier les sources de données mobilisables pour objectiver ces schémas, de qualifier les points de fragilité et d'apprécier leur variabilité selon les typologies de bâtiments et les configurations d'acteurs.

Dans un troisième temps, des stratégies prospectives low-tech de maintenance et d'entretien seront proposées et instruites. Il s'agira de construire des scénarios contrastés, d'évaluer leur capacité à réduire la vulnérabilité technique, économique et sociale des opérations de maintenance dans un contexte d'adaptation au changement climatique, et d'en discuter la faisabilité et l'acceptabilité avec les parties prenantes concernées.

Verrous scientifiques :

  • Définition et opérationnalisation de la notion de dépendance appliquée à la maintenance du bâti, au-delà de la seule dépendance à la ressource (savoirs, acteurs, organisations, réseaux)

  • Caractérisation et représentation de schémas de dépendance à l'échelle urbaine, à partir de données hétérogènes et partiellement indisponibles

  • Évaluation prospective de stratégies low-tech en l'absence de retours d'expérience consolidés et de métriques établies

  • Articulation interdisciplinaire entre sciences de l'ingénieur et sciences humaines et sociales, et capacité à répliquer l'approche tout en visant la « parcimonie » des méthodes et modèles

Objectifs de développement durable rattachés :

title: Manufacturing Engineer – Magnet Industrialisation
description:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

TEAM & ROLE

  • Architect a breakthrough energy technology – Play a defining role in designing and integrating the systems that will power the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion plant, influencing decisions that shape the future of clean energy.

  • Solve some of the most complex engineering challenges in fusion – Work across magnet design, HTS technology, manufacturing, structural integration, and controls, turning cutting-edge science into real hardware

  • Move fast and build what matters – Join a highly ambitious, multidisciplinary team that combines cutting-edge simulation with hands-on engineering, turning bold ideas into real hardware on the path to commercial fusion.

WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION

  • You will get to work on some of the most complex tech challenges to bring abundant, safe, clean energy to the world.

  • You'll get to join and learn from an exceptional selection of accomplished and driven individuals.

  • Do your life’s best work and enjoy the journey.

  • Get to show that big things are possible in Europe when you assemble the best talent.

YOUR IMPACT

You will support the industrialisation of production processes for magnet production, contributing directly to the execution of key activities within Proxima’s magnet program.

You will play a central role in designing, testing and scaling up a wide array of production processes such as welding, bonding, sealing and coating.

You will be part of the team bridging manufacturing technology for first prototypes to full scale manufacturing

You will operate across a wide range of technical tasks, from design and engineering to hands on production work, and collaborating closely with engineers and technicians

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Define the requirements for industrialised manufacturing equipment and processes, to ensure performance, repeatability and safe operation

  • Contribute to the development of in process monitoring and non destructive testing

  • Help to determine and justify quality requirements to ensure smooth manufacturing while keeping the required product performance

  • Design jigs and tools for magnet industrialised production

  • Collaborate closely with engineers and technicians across multiple teams

WHO YOU ARE

  • A master´s degree in mechanical, mechatronics or similar engineering field

  • A wide experience in manufacturing process development, process monitoring and non destructive testing in an industrial setting

  • Strong hands-on experience in production environments over a wide range of production processes (for ex. welding, machining, assembly, bonding)

  • Hands on experience in prototyping and testing

  • Proficient in creating development plans from start to finish for a new process

  • Experience in trouble-shooting issues as they arise on production lines

  • Ability to work across a variety of tasks in a dynamic environment

  • Reliable, proactive, and solution-oriented mindset

  • Strong team player, able to collaborate closely with engineers and technical staff

  • A high performer who loves challenges and is not afraid to experiment, take risks and learn from mistakes.

NICE TO HAVE

  • Familiarity in both prototype manufacturing and industrial manufacturing

  • Comfortable with CAD: good knowledge of Catia V5 or 3DExperience are considered as a plus

  • A background in product testing and qualification in a regulated industry is a plus

  • Exposure to SCADA systems or MES integration

  • Knowledge of safety standards and risk assessments in automated environments

title: Numerical Modeling Engineer
description:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

TEAM AND ROLE

  • Architect a breakthrough energy technology – Play a defining role in designing and integrating the systems that will power the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion plant, influencing decisions that shape the future of clean energy.

  • Solve some of the most complex engineering challenges in fusion – Work across magnet design, HTS technology, manufacturing, structural integration, and controls, turning cutting-edge science into real hardware

  • Move fast and build what matters – Join a highly ambitious, multidisciplinary team that combines cutting-edge simulation with hands-on engineering, turning bold ideas into real hardware on the path to commercial fusion.

WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION

Impact: Your simulations will directly shape the magnets that enable commercial fusion energy.

Ownership: As part of a small, highly technical team, you will define modeling standards and influence core design decisions.

Frontier Engineering: Work at the intersection of high-field electromagnetics, cryogenics, and advanced numerical methods.

Collaboration: Join a team combining deep superconducting expertise with advanced computational capability to solve one of the hardest engineering challenges of our time.

YOUR IMPACT

At Proxima Fusion, we are designing the first generation of fusion power plants to provide the world with clean, carbon-free energy. The heart of our reactor lies in its superconducting coils. These magnets operate at cryogenic temperatures, generate extreme magnetic fields, and must remain stable under complex electromagnetic and thermal transients.

We are looking for a Numerical Modeling Engineer to develop high-fidelity simulation tools that predict and de-risk the behavior of our superconducting magnets. Your work will span electromagnetic, thermal, and transient multiphysics modeling - including quench dynamics - and will directly inform design decisions for conductors, coils, and protection systems.

This role is not about running black-box simulations. It is about building robust numerical frameworks - combining commercial multiphysics tools with in-house developed models - to enable fast, reliable, physics-driven engineering decisions.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

Your work will combine physics modeling, numerical implementation, and close collaboration with magnet designers and experimental teams. You will contribute across three primary domains:

1. Electromagnetic & Thermal Multiphysics Modeling

You will develop predictive models of superconducting magnet behavior across steady-state and transient regimes.

  • Electromagnetic Simulation: Model high-field magnet systems including current distribution, inductance, AC losses, and nonlinear material behavior.

  • Thermal Modeling: Simulate heat generation, conduction, and cryogenic cooling performance under operational and fault conditions.

  • Multiphysics Coupling: Develop coupled EM-thermal models to capture transient events such as current redistribution and localized heating.

  • Quench Modeling: Implement and validate numerical frameworks to simulate quench initiation, propagation, and protection strategies.

  • Model Validation: Correlate simulations with experimental data from conductor and coil tests to continuously refine predictive capability.

2. In-House Tool Development & Numerical Infrastructure

Beyond commercial software, you will help build Proxima’s internal modeling backbone.

  • Custom Solvers & Reduced-Order Models: Develop fast, scalable modeling tools for system-level studies and design iteration.

  • Automation & Parametric Studies: Build robust pipelines for design sweeps, optimization, and uncertainty quantification.

  • Code Development: Contribute to internal Python- or C++-based frameworks for magnet modeling and data post-processing.

  • Verification & Benchmarking: Establish numerical best practices, validation procedures, and cross-comparison between tools.

  • Scalability: Ensure models can scale from conductor-level physics to full magnet assemblies.

Experience with COMSOL or similar commercial multiphysics tools (ANSYS, Opera, etc.) is valuable, but building reliable, physics-based in-house tools is equally (if not more) important.

3. Design Integration & Engineering Decision Support

Your models will not live in isolation — they will directly shape hardware.

  • Design Feedback: Provide quantitative guidance on conductor layout, stabilization strategies, and protection schemes.

  • Risk Assessment: Identify failure modes and quantify margins under realistic operating scenarios.

  • Cross-Team Collaboration: Work closely with magnet engineers, quench protection specialists, and test engineers.

  • Documentation & Communication: Translate complex physics into clear engineering recommendations.

WHO YOU ARE

We are looking for a rigorous numerical thinker who enjoys bridging fundamental physics and practical engineering.

Background:

  • Degree (MSc or PhD) in Electrical Engineering, Applied Physics, Computational Engineering, or a related field.

Core Expertise:

  • Strong foundation in electromagnetics and physics-based numerical modeling (e.g., FEM, nonlinear coupled systems), with the ability to implement and extend models programmatically

  • Experience with multiphysics and transient simulations (e.g., electromagnetic–thermal coupling, fast transients).

  • Proficiency in at least one scientific programming language (Python, MATLAB, C++, or similar), with interest in developing internal modeling tools and workflows.

Valued Experience (not all required):

  • Electromagnetic numerical modeling

  • COMSOL or other commercial FEM tools.

  • Modeling of high-current or high-field devices.

  • Thermal modeling and heat transfer in complex systems.

  • Experience building internal engineering tools rather than relying purely on GUI-based workflows.

Mindset:

  • You question assumptions and validate results critically.

  • You are comfortable building models from first principles.

  • You thrive in a startup environment where tools, processes, and standards are still evolving.

Prior experience with superconductors or HTS magnets is a plus - but strong electromagnetic and numerical expertise is the primary requirement.

title: VP, Growth
description:
About Nivoda

Nivoda is the operating system for the global jewellery industry. Our B2B marketplace connects jewellery retailers with diamond, gemstone and jewellery suppliers in 70+ countries, and we process $300M+ in annual transactions in a $350B industry that has barely been touched by technology.

We remove the traditional barriers of capital, geography and information asymmetry. An independent jeweller in Ohio can source from a cutter in Mumbai with the same ease, pricing and confidence as one of the world's largest chains. That's the whole point.

Our Mission 🚀

Diamond and gemstone trading has run on inefficiency, opacity and exclusivity for generations. Relationships were gatekept, pricing was hidden, and the size of your business decided the terms you got. We're building the infrastructure that changes that — so any jewellery business, anywhere, regardless of size, can compete on the quality of what they do rather than who they know.

The Marketing Team ⭐️

We're a remote-first, low-hierarchy company where the best idea wins. Marketing at Nivoda is at an inflection point: we have real product-market fit, thousands of businesses transacting, a category we have the opportunity to redefine, and a marketing function that has not yet been built to match the scale of the opportunity.

About the Role

We're hiring a VP of Growth to build Nivoda's marketing function from the ground up and turn it into a predictable growth engine for a two-sided global marketplace.

This is a builder's role, not a caretaker's or maintainer’s. You'll own the strategy, the growth model, the budget, the team and the number. You'll be the person who decides what Nivoda's category story is in partnership with the CEO, how we reach tens of thousands of independent jewellers and suppliers, and how we prove — with data, not decks — which of those bets are working.

You'll report directly to the President and sit on the senior leadership team, with a mandate that spans demand generation, product marketing, brand, content, lifecycle and marketing operations across every market we trade in.

What would you be doing?

  • Owning Nivoda's marketing strategy end to end - translating company goals into a growth model, then into the channels, programmes and headcount that deliver it

  • Building the marketing team from its current base: hiring, structuring and levelling up a global team, and building the systems, briefs and feedback loops that make good marketers great

  • Owning demand generation and pipeline contribution for both sides of the marketplace - retailers who need supply, and suppliers who need demand

  • Building the measurement layer: attribution, funnel instrumentation, CAC and payback by segment and geography, and a reporting rhythm the leadership team actually trusts

  • Running marketing as a portfolio of experiments rather than a calendar of campaigns - defining leading indicators, killing what doesn't work quickly, and going all-in on what does

  • Owning positioning and product marketing across a multi-product platform (diamonds, gemstones, melee, bridal, finished jewellery, payments and logistics) so each launch lands with the right segment

  • Building the category narrative for "the operating system for the jewellery industry" - and making Nivoda the default name in an industry that still runs on WhatsApp and trade shows

  • Driving lifecycle and retention marketing in partnership with Product: onboarding, activation, reactivation and share-of-wallet growth inside existing accounts

  • Partnering closely with Sales and Revenue leadership on segmentation, ICP definition, territory support and sales enablement - marketing that helps close, not just fill the top

  • Localising go-to-market across our biggest markets, from the US and UK to India, Europe and Asia, without fragmenting the brand

  • Owning the marketing budget and making a clear, defensible case for where every dollar goes and what it returned

  • Representing marketing at leadership and board level - bringing a point of view on where growth comes from next, and the evidence behind it

What do we need from you?

  • Significant experience leading marketing in B2B SMB - selling to owner-operators and small businesses, not enterprise procurement committees. You understand that a high-volume, lower-ACV motion is a fundamentally different sport

  • A track record of building marketing teams and functions from the ground up. You've been the first or second marketing leader, hired the team, chosen the stack and created the operating model. Maintaining someone else's machine is not what you're looking for

  • Deep, hands-on data and growth orientation. You build growth models, instrument funnels, run experiments with real statistical discipline, and can talk fluently about CAC, payback, conversion by stage and cohort behaviour. You're as comfortable in the numbers as you are in the narrative

title: Brand Designer
description:
🍇 About grape: 
 
Our entrepreneurial spirit drives us in what we do and what we are passionate about. Our mission is to become the premier health partner in the insurance business. Recognising the need for innovation in the traditional employee insurance model we are set to revolutionize the employee insurance industry. We help companies support people before and after they get sick and to make more of their time. Our insurance solutions reduce monotonous and manual work for employees, doctors, HR & payroll managers. As we strive to lead a technology-driven transformation, we put employees first.
 
At grape we pride ourselves on our people and our culture. We continue to grow fast and that’s where you come in. Our team is dynamic, diverse and full of creative ideas. Want to join? We can’t wait to get to know you!

Your role:

Hi there. Janine here. I know, this is unconventional… I'm deviating from the regular job description script. Why? Because this role is different. The starting point for this role is different. And we want to communicate that clearly.

If you browse our website and think, "amazing opportunity for a rebrand", we are not for you. Because here's the truth: what you just saw isn't a draft. It's not a v1. It's the result of a year spent getting the fundamentals right and building a visual foundation we believe in for the long term. What you saw is the floor, not the ceiling. It's the minimum bar for anything we ship from here on out. No rebrand. No reset. Just continuous improvement.

We're now at the point where we're looking to build up in-house design, and we need someone who can put the brand before personal signature, buy into what you just saw, execute on it with the same care it was built with, and then, over the years, shape its trajectory and help develop it further.

Who are you designing for, you ask? Three very different audiences: HR, the CFO, and, most importantly, the insured person. Not the easiest of brief, since most of the industry still talks to people like they're a policy number, especially at their hardest moments. We want to change that. This is why your work matters so much. At every touchpoint. You're not just making things look good. You're deciding what it feels like to face this system on a day when someone has less capacity than usual to deal with it.

That's the job: breathe life into our brand with your design skills and branding expertise, ensuring we deliver high-quality design solutions that connect with our audiences, feel distinctively human, and feel distinctively us. 

The team, you ask?
At this stage of growth, most of us are generalists wearing many different hats each day. Outside of work, you might find us boating on the lake, snowboarding in Arosa, hiking in Appenzell, playing dress-up with our kids, or looking out the window in a classroom in Bern. A bunch of wonderful human beings, skilled in many different things in life. Each one is equally important in building this brand step by step, day by day.

P.S. No AI in the application process for this role! We look at every portfolio and read every cover letter. So, you are not wasting your time telling us why you want to join :)

Please add a link to your portfolio or attach it when applying.


What you’ll do:
  • Shape the brand story going forward.
  • Execute on our new visual identity and help sharpen our brand guidelines.
  • Lead design projects from concept through delivery.
  • Bring your creative expertise and know-how to campaign planning just as much as to execution.
  • Design and create digital and physical collateral for brand and marketing initiatives. 
  • Review design work from external partners to ensure high quality and brand consistency.

    • What you’ll need:
  • You bring +6 years of experience, either from a branding/ creative agency or working within an in-house team.
  • You have a proven track record of building brands, are able to adapt your designs to the respective brand, and are proficient at reviewing design materials to ensure cohesive execution.
  • You are equally skilled in creative direction and creative execution, taking ownership and occasionally working with freelancers to speed up the process.
  • Your strong aesthetic sensibility and passion for branding allow you to interpret the brand and deliver a unified narrative through your work.
  • You excel at managing a variety of design projects simultaneously, collaborating effectively with both internal teams and external stakeholders.
  • You are highly skilled in Figma and equally adept with Adobe InDesign, Illustrator, and Photoshop. After Effects is a plus.
  • Creating animated digital assets that are versatile and impactful is second nature to you.
  • You have an eye for detail, precision, and exceptional typography skills.
  • While you thrive working independently, you also enjoy partnering with diverse teams to bring projects and campaigns to life.
  • As a collaborator, you challenge others constructively while pushing your own creative boundaries.
  • You are fluent in English, both written and spoken, with German being a plus.

    • What you will learn:
  • Refine expertise in brand storytelling by working on diverse design projects that bring the grape brand’s vision to life across various platforms.
  • Expand skills in cross-functional collaboration through hands-on involvement with internal teams, external freelancers, and other stakeholders to ensure seamless execution of creative initiatives.
  • Deepen proficiency in creating scalable design systems that support cohesive branding and elevate the user experience across digital and physical touchpoints.
  • Gain exposure to strategic branding challenges by contributing to high-impact projects and learning how to adapt designs to evolving business needs and audience expectations.
    • 🤝 What we offer in return:
    🌱 Empowering workplace: Join a passionate team and an empowering workplace where you are given the ownership, tools, and support to make decisions and take initiative. Together we grow and build innovative solutions.
    💻  Hybrid setup: Enjoy the flexibility of our hybrid work schedule, with the freedom to work remotely or from our office in Zurich. On Thursdays, our team day, we meet together in our Zurich office.
    🪑 Home office stipend: To enable our hybrid setup, we allocate a one-off CHF 200.- home office budget to help you set up your dream workspace in the comfort of your own home.
    🌐 Internet allowance: We give you a monthly internet allowance to help cover your internet costs at home and enable you to work seamlessly from your home office.
    ⏳ Flexible working time: You can distribute your working hours the way you want to.
    🧠 Learning budget: We support you in improving your skills, acquiring new knowledge and advancing your career. We also allocate a CHF 1'500.- budget annually
    ❤️‍🩹  Well-being: Work-life balance is important to us and we foster a supportive work environment. We support you with mental health sessions with our partner Aepsy.
    🎫  Team events: Every month we gather for fun and engaging events where we can connect and bond with our colleagues and our teams.
    ✈️  Team retreats: Once a year we travel somewhere nice to bond with our colleagues.
    🚂  Travel and commute: We will cover your SBB half fare card, so we can spend some time together in the office.
    🌴 Paid vacation: You get 5 weeks (25 days) of paid vacation every year and 2 additional days of paid vacation to compensate for canton-related holidays, religious holidays, birthdays, etc. The total amount of paid vacation days per year is 27 days.
    🧖‍♀️ Wellness budget: Health and well-being looks different for everyone. You can optimize your wellness budget to best fit your needs.
    👨‍👨‍👦‍👦 Parental and adoptive leave: We offer additional time off to support employees who are balancing family and work time in the most crucial stages of family life.
    ✈️ Digital nomad: For every 3 years of employment, you can work for an extended period of time from anywhere in the world (location subject to review).
     
    🏁 Our recruitment process
    We place particular emphasis on four areas when making our selection decision: professional and technical skills, mindset & values. We evaluate these through the following steps:
     
    Step 1 - Your motivation
    To get to know you better, we invite you to a 30-minute motivational interview with our Talent Acquisition Team.
    Step 2 - Role fit
    In the first interview, we assess how well your qualifications and skills align with the role requirements. This discussion will take place with your Hiring Manager.
    Step 3 - Case study
    For roles with higher technical demands, we will invite you to complete a case study or technical assessment. This allows us to better evaluate your specific skills and problem-solving abilities.
    Step 4 - Our culture connect
    Throughout the interview process, you'll gain insight into our company culture, and we'll explore how your values and mindset align with our ways of working. The final interview will offer a deeper look into this connection, along with broader discussions about the role and our vision.
     
    Our diverse experiences, perspectives, and voices make us the company we are, and we would love to learn more about you!
    --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    Health is our foundation. Innovation drives our mission. Together, we’re building the future of employee insurance.
    At grape, collaboration isn’t just a buzzword, it’s the foundation of how we work, live, and succeed. From bold brainstorms and lessons learned, we overcome challenges side by side. Our time together is our greatest asset. Disrupting an industry that truly needs change takes courage, creativity, and team spirit and that’s exactly what defines us.
    With well-being at the core, we foster an environment where ideas and people thrive. Your growth matters as much as our mission. Whether it’s supporting your self-care, developing new solutions, or redefining how health and insurance connect, we grow together.
    Our values guide us every step of the way: keeping Health at Heart, Inventing Together, and always striving to Embrace Clarity.

description:
Camunda is the enterprise platform for agentic orchestration, enabling organizations to coordinate AI agents, people, and systems across complex, end-to-end business processes. With built-in governance, auditability, and human oversight, Camunda gives enterprises the control they need to move AI from pilots to production — safely and at scale. Fully remote and global, we are in the middle of something bigger: transforming into an AI-first organisation, built on our own platform. We use Agentic AI to automate, orchestrate intelligent processes, and elevate human contribution across every team.

Named GP Bullhound’s Top 100 Next Unicorn list, 2025 Great Place to Work certified. Visionary in 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Business Orchestration and Automation Technologies. ranked 3rd in Flexa's 2026 Most Flexible Companies, We’re growing fast and looking for top talent to join our team. If you want meaningful work, visible impact and put something genuinely rare on your CV, keep reading.

About the role:

We're hiring for Self-Managed Experience (SMX) — the team responsible for making Camunda 8 deployable in a self-service way for customers who run their own infrastructure. SMX covers two areas of work: installation artifacts (Helm chart, Docker Compose, C8Run) and reference architectures & cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, Azure).

This role sits primarily on the installation artifacts side — building, maintaining, and releasing the artifacts that ship Camunda 8 to every self-managed customer. You'll be fully embedded in that area day-to-day, but you'll work alongside the reference-architecture side of the team regularly, and SMX is actively working toward enabling every engineer to review and contribute across both stacks over time.

SMX is also shifting from a purely artifact- and ops-focused team toward one in which engineers bring customer judgment and product sense alongside technical depth. That means engaging directly with the teams closest to customers — Support, Consulting, Presales — and using that signal to help shape what we prioritize, not just executing a fully-specced ticket.

You'll find plenty of room to leave your own footprint: deployment automation, software and infrastructure testing, multi-region setups, and developer experience are all live areas of investment as the team matures from "basic install" toward full-lifecycle ownership (upgrades, backup/restore, disaster recovery).

Curious about the kind of challenges you'll work on at Camunda? Watch this quick 30-minute talk from our engineers to learn more about the new Camunda Exporter and how we’re solving complex problems at scale

What You’ll Be Doing:

  •  Build, maintain, and release C8 distribution artifacts for self-managed customers — Helm Charts (Kubernetes), C8Run, and Docker Compose — along with their documentation.

  • Improve the reliability and usability of deployment artifacts across the full customer lifecycle: installation, upgrades, and day-2 operations, not just initial deployment.

  • Engage directly with internal customer-facing teams (Support, Consulting, Presales) to understand real deployment problems, and use that signal to help shape what gets prioritized — not just how it gets built. Collaborate with Development Teams, Product Management, QA, and Documentation to ship integrated, tested, and documented releases.

  • Take part in the team's shared medic rotation and resolve engineering-level support cases, feeding learnings back into development.

  • Contribute to the shared tooling (review, deployment, and test tooling) that SMX is building so other Camunda teams can adopt it — this is one of the team's current investment areas.

What success looks like (first ~3 months):

  • Taken on your first medic rotation slot and support tickets to understand the stack, customer challenges, and deployment environments.

  • Improved onboarding or documentation, turning your own ramp-up experience into concrete improvements.

  • Contributed to artifact fixes, CI/CD enhancements, or test automation that strengthens release quality.

  • Deliver structural improvement initiatives — a feature request, or a test/release improvement.

  • Built working relationships with engineering, QA, and product peers, and started building context on the reference-architecture side of the team.

  • Started forming your own view of a customer pain point from firsthand signal (support tickets, consulting feedback), not just from a ticket description.

What You Bring:

  • Ability and/or willingness to use our product, with genuine curiosity about the customer problem behind a ticket — comfortable asking "should we build this" as well as "how do we build this."

  • Strong expertise in building, operating, and maintaining Helm Charts; deploying applications on Kubernetes; implementing CI/CD pipelines with GitHub Actions; and managing infrastructure as code (e.g., Terraform).

  • Ability to create clear technical documentation and communicate effectively across teams.

  • A pragmatic and autonomous approach to programming and problem-solving.

  • You thrive as a manager of one — you build it, you own it — and take pride in delivering maintainable, operable software.

 Nice-to-haves:

  • Experience running and operating on-prem/self-hosted software on Docker.

  • Familiarity with Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, or similar observability tools.

  • Working knowledge of the Go programming language.

  • Exposure to cloud infrastructure/IaC (Terraform, Crossplane) — useful as SMX moves toward shared review capability across installation artifacts and reference architectures.

  • Proficiency in Python, Go, or similar languages – You write scripts and automation tools that solve real problems.

  • Experience with SLOs and alerting frameworks – You've helped teams define meaningful service level objectives and set up alerts that don't cry wolf.

Today, customers have no first-class way to stream their own process data out of Camunda, and Camunda's own analytics product is bottlenecked by querying the same storage the live engine depends on. You'll be part of a greenfield team rebuilding how process data is consumed and served at scale, built on top of a durable, continuously-written streaming layer that decouples data consumption from the live engine. You'll be part of a small team from day one, with real room to shape both the architecture and the team's scope as it matures.

At Camunda, we approach engineering in a holistic manner. As such, you will form strong partnerships with product management, the Data Layer and Distributed Systems teams, QA, and support, and work closely with your peers to not only deliver but directly influence how our data streaming architecture evolves to meet our customers' needs.

What You Will Do:

  • Help rebuild how Camunda's analytics product consumes and serves process data at scale, moving it off the engine's critical path entirely.

  • Design and build the core streaming infrastructure that decouples process data access from the live execution engine, backed by durable, object storage.

  • Build customer-facing data streaming capabilities, including a supported way to integrate with systems like Kafka, so customers can reliably get their process data into their own tools.

  • Make foundational architecture decisions as part of a small, high-ownership team, including how the system guarantees consistency and durability across a distributed streaming pipeline.

  • Participate in L3 support and on-call rotations, partnering with Support and SRE to investigate data layer production issues, and feeding what you learn back into the product.
